drug_class: Antidiarrheal (opioid receptor agonist acting on the gut)
purpose: Loperamide is used to help control and relieve diarrhea, including traveler's diarrhea. It helps slow down how often you need to go to the bathroom and makes your stools firmer. It can also be used by people with certain bowel conditions like inflammatory bowel disease to help manage ongoing diarrhea.
how_it_works: Loperamide works by slowing down the movement of your intestines so food and liquid move through your gut more slowly. This gives your body more time to absorb water from your stool, making it less loose and watery. It also reduces the urge to go to the bathroom. Unlike some other medicines in its class, it does not enter the brain, so it does not cause a high or make you feel drowsy.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include constipation, stomach pain or cramping, nausea, dizziness, and bloating. These are usually mild and go away on their own as your diarrhea gets better.
warnings: Do not take more than the recommended dose — taking too much loperamide can cause serious, life-threatening heart rhythm problems. Do not use it if you have blood in your stool or a high fever, as these may be signs of a more serious infection that needs medical treatment. Stop using it and see a doctor if diarrhea lasts more than 2 days in adults or if symptoms get worse. Keep out of reach of children, and never give adult doses to young children.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual starting dose for acute diarrhea is 4 mg (two 2 mg capsules or tablets) right away, then 2 mg after each loose stool, but no more than 16 mg per day. For traveler's diarrhea, the maximum is 8 mg per day without a doctor's guidance. Always follow the directions on the package or as your doctor tells you.
